subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Regeneration: Recycling Heat Inside Engines
description: One-minute skill: Regeneration: Recycling Heat Inside Engines.

hook.text: Exhaust gas leaves an engine hot. Capturing that heat to preheat incoming air wastes less fuel.

buildup.text: A regenerator is a heat exchanger that transfers thermal energy from the hot exhaust to the cold intake.

discovery.text: The burner now heats air that's already warm. Less fuel is needed to reach operating temperature. Efficiency climbs.

twist.text: Regenerators add weight, cost, and complexity. For jet engines that need to be light, they aren't worth it.

climax.text: Stationary gas turbines and Stirling engines benefit most. When weight doesn't matter, regeneration shines.

punchline.text: Why throw away hot exhaust? Use it to preheat the next batch.

quiz.question: Why don't jet engines typically use regenerators?
options: Jet fuel burns too hot for any heat exchanger to withstand
The added weight and complexity outweigh the efficiency gains in aircraft
Jet engines already operate at 100% of Carnot efficiency
